market_question: Iran closes its airspace by June 30?
reasoning: The market implies a 57.5% chance of a major non-weather airspace closure by mid-2026, which appears too high. Historical closures occur roughly once every 2–4 years; over a 15-month window, a base rate of ~30% seems more realistic. While regional tensions persist, a broad closure affecting multiple major airports is not the norm.
evidence_points: Only two major closures (2020 after PS752 shootdown, 2024 western airspace during Iran-Israel strike) have occurred in the last five years.
The resolution requires a non-weather suspension impacting at least two of five named airports or a broad regional closure—far from routine.
Current geopolitical risk is elevated, but even in a conflict scenario, full closures are short-lived and may not meet the stringent definition.
sources_consulted: Flightradar24 and historical airspace closure records
